speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long you have noticed these skin lesions and if they are itchy or painful? 

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count: WBC 6,000 /μL, Hemoglobin 12 g/dL, Platelets 300,000 /μL

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Previously healthy, up-to-date immunizations, no significant illnesses. Social history: Attends daycare three times per week.

speaker: Patient
text: No fever, rash in other locations, itching, or systemic symptoms. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Do these lesions appear as blisters, scabs, or flat spots, and have you noticed anyone else in your home with similar symptoms? REQUEST TEST: Tzanck Smear. REQUEST IMAGES: Close-up of skin lesions.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Tzanck Smear: Negative for multinucleated giant cells or viral inclusions (consistent with Molluscum Contagiosum, not Herpes or Varicella); Images would show skin-colored, pearly papules with central umbilication.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for those results; the negative Tzanck smear and the description of pearly papules with central umbilication are highly suggestive of a specific viral infection. To confirm the extent of the lesions before finalizing the diagnosis, could you tell me approximately how many spots you have and where they are located on your body?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum Contagiosum
